An initial exploratory owned-file metadata query used unavailable os.listxattr on macOS and stopped before tar or publisher execution. It has no mutation verdict.

M17 and M25 original invalid attempts contain FileExistsError after failed subtests; M18 additionally contains JSONDecodeError from partial-publication stdout. Test-only fixture admission cleanup and assertion ordering corrected these runtime artifacts after the frozen first round.
limits: External gh, cosign and npm commands were controlled recording fixtures. No real download, Sigstore verification, registry query, OIDC authorization, install or publication occurred.
Archived payloads were owned synthetic inputs and were not executed. Actual local tar was executed; Windows7z was not installed or executed.
The source packaging fix and its separate metadata-removal negative control are not counted among the downstream25 or15 mutants.

The first workflow interpolation variant changes two downstream shell uses and is killed by the explicit no-expression source assertion while strict tag guards remain present; this is not claimed as a fresh command-execution exploit.
Eleven original replay patches were applied unchanged. The ZIP type variant was retargeted to the corrected metadata guard, with both exact patches preserved.

The independent scope is the30-method publication core. The evolving required-module CI admission gate is separately reviewed and tested by the root team; its39-method run is not claimed as this reviewer's execution.

Successful npm preflight is not a transaction across remote packages. A later real publication failure may leave earlier packages published; the helper preserves matching existing versions on a fresh retry.
Real platform builds, signing, release creation, tag movement and remote publication remain outside this review.
